newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Robotics jumps as modem talk resumes.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Robotics jumps as modem talk resumes.

text.p: Shares of modem-maker U.S. Robotics Corp jumped 6-7/8 to 72-3/4 on Thursday as talk surfaced again that the company is preparing to unveil a faster-speed modem.
"The whispers are they're going to announce the high-speed modem soon," said Southcoast Capital analyst Jim McIlree.

A U.S. Robotics spokeswoman said the company has not released any statements and is not aware of any new analysts' reports. She repeated, however, the company's stance that the 33.6 kilobit per second modem currently in the market is not the fatest possible.
"We have not announced anything and we have nothing to announce," said U.S. Robotics spokeswoman Karen Novak. "(W)e believe 33.6 is not the end of the line."
But McIlree and options traders said they are awaiting more details from U.S. Robotics, which holds a dominant market share in modems.

Other companies, for example, have set dates. Motorola Inc has said it will unveil a modem with 56 kbps capabilities in 1997, and Rockwell International Corp has said it expects to demonstrate 56 kbps technology at a trade show in November.

"This would be a very significant new cycle for them," McIlree said, referring to U.S. Robotics. "It would have a large impact on their desktop modem business and it would have a significant effect on their network systems business."
